evidence: Concrete conditional path: (1) A user session closes, creating transcript work under DESIGN-NOTES.md:241 and CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32. (2) With no occupant, graph activates the ordinary summarizer seat and posts a durable request (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34; DESIGN-NOTES.md:247-258). (3) Its occupant dispatches processing and reports completion, then its own native session closes. The design tracks native sessions and never defines whether this ordinary seat's transcript is ineligible (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:7,10,32-34; DESIGN-NOTES.md:241,253-259). If eligible, that closure creates a fresh request; graph reactivates the unoccupied summarizer, and each later closure repeats even though user work is complete. This contradicts the intended cheap dormancy and no recurring reasoning for ordinary bookkeeping (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:60,133; SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:93). Recursion is conditional, not an observed runtime failure. Choosing exclusion, routing, or another finite eligibility rule is an acknowledged unfinished transcript-lifecycle design detail, but is material to the approved automatic-activation path.
